symptoms: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions on leaves with whitish-grey centers and dark brown/reddish margins.
In advanced infection, dark necrotic lesions at the panicle neck (neck blast) causing chaffy grains or broken panicles.

severity_thresholds.low: < 5% leaf area affected with isolated leaf lesions and no neck/node involvement.
severity_thresholds.moderate: 5%–25% leaf area affected or > 5% tillers showing active expanding lesions.
severity_thresholds.severe: > 25% leaf area affected, coalescing blight, or any panicle neck/node blast infection.

cultural_organic_control: Avoid excessive split top-dressing of nitrogenous fertilizer (urea), which promotes succulent blast-susceptible foliage.
Maintain field sanitation by removing collateral weed hosts on bunds and avoiding severe water stress.
Seed/root-dip bio-management with Pseudomonas fluorescens as recommended in local SAU/ICAR Package of Practices.

approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Active foliar blast at moderate incidence or preventive boot/heading spray in endemic belts
approved_chemical_options.cibrc_aligned_note: CIB&RC registered fungicide for paddy blast management.
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Apply only if moderate/severe ETL is crossed. Verify exact CIB&RC label dilution and Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) on the container or with local KVK/DAO before spraying; wear PPE and avoid drift to water bodies.

approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Panicle emergence / neck blast risk stage
approved_chemical_options.cibrc_aligned_note: Combination systemic fungicide registered for paddy blast/sheath diseases.
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Rotate FRAC fungicide groups to delay resistance. Confirm exact label dosage and PHI with local KVK before application.

region_notes.general: Favored by high relative humidity (>85%), prolonged leaf wetness/dew, cloudy weather, and high nitrogen doses.
region_notes.Eastern India & Coastal: Monitor closely during Kharif tillering and Boro booting in Assam, West Bengal, Odisha, and coastal Andhra.
region_notes.North-Western Plains: High blast susceptibility reported in Basmati varieties across Punjab, Haryana, and Western UP.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate immediately to local KVK if neck/node blast appears at panicle emergence or >25% leaf area is blighted.
disease_pest_cards.source_reference: ICAR-IIRR / DPPQS IPM Package for Rice

symptoms: Circular to oval dark brown spots on leaves with a yellow halo around the margin.
Severe infection causes black discoloration on glumes/grains and poor grain filling.

severity_thresholds.low: < 5% leaf area covered by small discrete brown spots.
severity_thresholds.moderate: 5%–20% leaf area affected with spots coalescing on lower/middle leaves.
severity_thresholds.severe: > 20% leaf area affected or widespread spikelet/grain discoloration at flowering.

cultural_organic_control: Correct underlying soil nutrient deficiency (especially potassium, silicon, and zinc) based on a Soil Health Card test.
Use disease-free certified seed and perform hot-water or Pseudomonas bio-priming prior to nursery sowing.
Avoid sudden drought stress by maintaining shallow uniform moisture during active tillering.

approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Moderate foliar spread or boot-leaf protection against grain spotting
approved_chemical_options.cibrc_aligned_note: CIB&RC-approved fungicide options for rice brown spot.
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Brown spot is strongly linked to nutrient/moisture stress; address soil fertility first. Confirm exact label dosage and PHI with local KVK/DAO and wear protective gear.

region_notes.general: Historically severe in nutrient-poor, rainfed upland, or moisture-stressed paddy soils.
region_notes.Eastern & Central India: Common in rainfed shallow lowlands of Bihar, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and West Bengal.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate to KVK for soil nutrient diagnostics if brown spot persists across consecutive seasons or affects >20% foliage.
disease_pest_cards.source_reference: ICAR-IIRR / DPPQS IPM Package for Rice

symptoms: Water-soaked yellow-to-straw-colored stripes starting from leaf tips and margins with wavy inner edges.
Early morning bacterial ooze droplets on young lesions that dry into yellowish beads.

severity_thresholds.low: < 5% leaf area showing marginal blighting on older leaves.
severity_thresholds.moderate: 5%–20% leaf area blighted across localized field patches.
severity_thresholds.severe: > 20% leaf area blighted or Kresek (systemic seedling/tiller wilting) observed.

cultural_organic_control: Drain standing water temporarily and withhold nitrogen top-dressing immediately upon first BLB detection.
Avoid moving irrigation water from infected plots into healthy downstream paddy fields.
Clip leaf tips only if healthy; avoid mechanical injury during weeding in wet conditions.

approved_chemical_options.active_ingredient: Copper Hydroxide 53.8% DF or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP
approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Early localized focus spread (fungicides like Tricyclazole/Carbendazim are ineffective against bacteria)
approved_chemical_options.cibrc_aligned_note: Bactericidal copper formulation; verify current state KVK advisory on bactericides.
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Standard fungal sprays do not control bacterial blight. Confirm locally approved bactericide protocol and label dosage with KVK/DAO; avoid routine antibiotic misuse.

region_notes.general: Triggered by monsoon storms, leaf wounding, high nitrogen, and stagnant standing water.
region_notes.Indo-Gangetic & Coastal Deltas: Frequent post-cyclone/heavy-rain outbreaks in Punjab, Haryana, UP, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate urgently to KVK if Kresek wilting appears or wavy blight spreads rapidly after storm damage.
disease_pest_cards.source_reference: ICAR-IIRR / DPPQS IPM Package for Rice

symptoms: Nymphs and brownish adults clustering at the basal stem near water level sucking plant sap.
Circular patches of yellowing, drying, and lodging plants known as 'hopper burn'.

severity_thresholds.low: < 5 hoppers per hill (monitor natural predators like spiders and mirid bugs).
severity_thresholds.moderate: 5–10 hoppers per hill at vegetative stage or 10–20 at panicle stage.
severity_thresholds.severe: > 10–20 hoppers per hill or visible circular hopper-burn patches.

cultural_organic_control: Drain standing field water for 3–4 days to expose basal stems and disrupt BPH microclimate.
Form alleyways (skipping 1 row every 8–10 rows) during planting/mid-season to improve aeration and light penetration.
Conserve natural enemies (wolf spiders, mirid bugs); avoid synthetic pyrethroids which trigger BPH resurgence.

approved_chemical_options.active_ingredient: Pymetrozine 50% WG or Dinotefuran 20% SG or Buprofezin 25% SC
approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Direct spray towards stem base only when ETL (10+ hoppers/hill) is exceeded
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Avoid broad-spectrum synthetic pyrethroids (cause pest resurgence). Direct nozzle to plant base; check label dosage, PHI, and bee/fish safety warnings with local KVK.

region_notes.general: Thrives in dense, heavily fertilized, continuously flooded paddy canopies.
region_notes.Godavari/Krishna & IGP Belts: Major late-Kharif and Rabi threat in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha, Punjab, and Haryana.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate immediately to KVK if hopper-burn patches appear or hopper counts exceed 15–20 per hill despite drainage.
disease_pest_cards.source_reference: ICAR-IIRR / DPPQS IPM Package for Rice

symptoms: Small, round to oval orange-brown pustules (uredia) scattered irregularly on the upper leaf surface.
Rusty orange spore powder rubs off easily on fingers when touched.

severity_thresholds.low: Trace to < 5% leaf area covered on lower leaves.
severity_thresholds.moderate: 5%–20% leaf area covered moving onto flag/upper leaves.
severity_thresholds.severe: > 20% leaf area covered on upper/flag leaves during booting or grain filling.

cultural_organic_control: Cultivate locally recommended rust-resistant wheat varieties (e.g., ICAR-IIWBR released varieties for your zone).
Avoid late sowing and excessive nitrogen application which prolong succulent foliage.
Scout fields weekly starting January–February for early foci.

approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Flag-leaf protection when pustules appear on upper canopy above trace levels
approved_chemical_options.cibrc_aligned_note: CIB&RC-registered triazole fungicides recommended by ICAR-IIWBR for wheat rusts.
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Do not spray if crop is near physiological maturity. Verify CIB&RC label dosage, PHI, and protective equipment requirements with local KVK.

region_notes.general: Favored by mild temperatures (15–25°C) and morning dew/humidity across wheat belts.
region_notes.Central & Peninsular India: Early appearance possible in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate to KVK/ICAR-IIWBR alert network if rust appears on flag leaves or on previously resistant cultivars.

symptoms: Bright yellow-to-lemon pustules arranged in narrow linear stripes parallel to leaf veins.
Yellow dust/spores stain clothing or fingers when brushing past infected leaves.

severity_thresholds.low: Isolated early foci (< 5% plants) in shaded/sub-mountainous pockets.
severity_thresholds.moderate: 5%–15% leaf severity spreading outward from initial foci.
severity_thresholds.severe: > 15% leaf severity or rapid multi-leaf epidemic spread before grain fill.

cultural_organic_control: Inspect field borders, poplar-shaded rows, and early-sown patches weekly during cool winter weather (10–18°C).
Remove/avoid susceptible varieties in sub-mountainous zones and adopt recommended varietal diversification.

approved_chemical_options.active_ingredient: Propiconazole 25% EC or Tebuconazole 25% WG or Azoxystrobin + Tebuconazole
approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Immediate spot-spraying around initial yellow rust foci to halt downwind spore spread
approved_chemical_options.cibrc_aligned_note: ICAR-IIWBR recommended rust fungicides for NWPZ stripe rust containment.
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Spot-spray foci promptly rather than waiting for field-wide spread. Confirm exact label dilution and PHI with local KVK/Agriculture Department.

region_notes.general: Cool-weather pathogen (10–20°C with fog/dew); spreads rapidly by wind.
region_notes.North-Western Plains & Hills: High priority surveillance in Punjab, Haryana, Himachal foothills, Uttarakhand, J&K, and Western UP.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate immediately to KVK/State Agriculture Department on first confirmed yellow rust focus to trigger regional containment.
disease_pest_cards.source_reference: ICAR-IIWBR Stripe Rust Surveillance & Management Guidelines

symptoms: Colonies of soft-bodied green/yellowish aphids clustering on earheads, flag leaves, and tender stems.
Sticky honeydew on leaves attracting black sooty mold and yellowing/shriveled grains.

severity_thresholds.low: < 5 aphids per earhead/tiller with ladybird beetles present.
severity_thresholds.moderate: 5–10 aphids per earhead/tiller on border rows.
severity_thresholds.severe: > 10 aphids per earhead/tiller across the main field during milky grain stage.

cultural_organic_control: Preserve natural predators (coccinellid ladybird beetles, syrphid flies, lacewings) — avoid unnecessary sprays below ETL.
Install yellow sticky traps along field borders for early monitoring.
Use neem-based formulation (Azadirachtin) on initial border colonies if predators are scarce.

approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Spray only when aphid count crosses ETL (>10 aphids/earhead) with low predator activity
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Do not spray if ladybird beetles are actively controlling small colonies. Follow label PHI and avoid spraying during pollinator foraging hours; verify dose with KVK.

region_notes.general: Typically builds up during February–March warming as wheat heads emerge.
region_notes.Punjab, Haryana, UP & Rajasthan: Often starts from field margins; border-only spraying frequently suffices.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate to KVK if aphid densities exceed 15–20 per earhead at grain filling or fail to respond to border management.
disease_pest_cards.source_reference: ICAR-IIWBR / DPPQS IPM Package for Wheat

symptoms: Circular bore holes in squares, flowers, and green bolls with larval frass (excreta) or flared/rosetted flowers.
Premature square/boll shedding and stained lint inside damaged bolls.

severity_thresholds.low: < 5% damaged squares/bolls or below pheromone trap threshold.
severity_thresholds.moderate: 5%–10% damaged fruiting bodies or >= 8–10 moths/trap/night for 3 consecutive nights.
severity_thresholds.severe: > 10% damaged bolls/squares or widespread pink bollworm rosette flowers across field.

cultural_organic_control: Install pheromone traps (5 traps/ha) to monitor adult moth catches and time interventions accurately.
Collect and destroy fallen infested squares/rosetted flowers and erect bird perches (10–15/ha).
Spray Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) or Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) / HaNPV against early-instar larvae.

approved_chemical_options.active_ingredient: Emamectin benzoate 5% SG or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC or Spinosad 45% SC
approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Early larval instar emergence coinciding with ETL crossing (5–10% damage)
approved_chemical_options.cibrc_aligned_note: CIB&RC-registered larvicides per ICAR-CICR resistance management guidelines.
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Never use banned insecticides or tank-mix arbitrary cocktails. Avoid repeated synthetic pyrethroid use early season; verify label dose, PHI, and IRAC rotation with local KVK.

region_notes.general: Pink bollworm resistance to Bt cotton has increased importance of pheromone monitoring and timely crop termination.
region_notes.Maharashtra, Gujarat, Telangana & Punjab: Follow state ICAR-CICR seasonal termination schedules and avoid extending ratoon/late cotton.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate to KVK immediately if bollworm infestation exceeds 10% green bolls or affects Bt-cotton hybrids.
disease_pest_cards.source_reference: ICAR-CICR / DPPQS Cotton IPM & Pink Bollworm Advisory

symptoms: Dense clusters of yellow-green to dark green aphids on tender shoots and leaf undersides.
Downward curling/crinkling of young leaves coated with shiny honeydew and black sooty mold.

severity_thresholds.low: < 10% plants infested with light shoot colonies and active predators.
severity_thresholds.moderate: 10%–20% plants showing leaf curling and honeydew deposition.
severity_thresholds.severe: > 20% plants severely stunted with heavy honeydew/sooty mold threatening open bolls.

cultural_organic_control: Avoid excessive nitrogenous fertilizer which increases lush sap-feeding attractiveness.
Conserve coccinellid predators and chrysopids; deploy yellow sticky traps for monitoring.
Apply neem-based botanicals (Azadirachtin 1500 ppm) during initial build-up.

approved_chemical_options.active_ingredient: Flonicamid 50% WG or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL or Acetamiprid 20% SP
approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Only when sucking pest ETL (15–20 aphids/leaf or >15% infested plants) is reached
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Wait until ETL is exceeded to protect beneficial predators and avoid whitefly flare-up. Spray during late afternoon to protect honeybees; confirm label dosage with KVK.

region_notes.general: Frequently peaks during dry spells following early monsoon or mid-vegetative growth.
region_notes.Central & Southern Cotton Zones: Monitor closely in rainfed black cotton soils of Vidarbha, Marathwada, Gujarat, and Telangana.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate to KVK if honeydew contaminates open lint or multiple sucking pests co-occur above ETL.
disease_pest_cards.source_reference: ICAR-CICR / DPPQS IPM Package for Cotton

symptoms: Tiny white moth-like insects rising in clouds from undersides of leaves when disturbed.
Yellowing leaves, sticky honeydew, black sooty mold, and potential Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuV) transmission.

severity_thresholds.moderate: 4–6 adults per leaf (approaching ETL of 6 adults/leaf).
severity_thresholds.severe: > 6–8 adults per leaf or heavy nymphal scales with sooty mold / leaf curl.

cultural_organic_control: Install yellow sticky traps (25–40/ha) and remove weed hosts (kanghi buti, peeli buti) on field bunds.
Spray Neem/NSKE 5% or fish oil rosin soap targeting leaf undersides early in infestation.
Avoid synthetic pyrethroids and tank mixes which trigger severe whitefly resurgence.

approved_chemical_options.active_ingredient: Pyriproxyfen 10% EC or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC or Diafenthiuron 50% WP
approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Egg/nymphal stages or adult ETL (>= 6 whiteflies/leaf) using thorough under-leaf coverage
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Strictly avoid unapproved insecticide mixtures and pyrethroids. Rotate modes of action, verify CIB&RC label dose/PHI with KVK, and protect pollinators.

region_notes.general: High humidity alternating with dry hot spells accelerates whitefly generations.
region_notes.North Cotton Zone: Critical vector of Cotton Leaf Curl Disease (CLCuD) in Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate urgently to KVK if whitefly exceeds 6–8 adults/leaf or leaf curl symptoms emerge.

symptoms: Irregular water-soaked dark green to purplish-black lesions on leaf tips/margins expanding rapidly.
White cottony fungal-like growth visible on the underside of lesions during humid mornings, accompanied by a characteristic rotting odor.

severity_thresholds.low: < 5% foliage affected in isolated plants under cool humid conditions.
severity_thresholds.moderate: 5%–15% foliage infected (rapid epidemic potential within 3–5 days).
severity_thresholds.severe: > 15% foliage blighted or stem lesions visible; high risk of tuber rot.

cultural_organic_control: Use certified blight-free seed tubers and destroy volunteer plants and cull piles.
Ensure proper earthing up (ridge height) to prevent zoospores washing onto tubers, and avoid over-irrigation during cloudy/foggy spells.
Rogue and bury isolated early-infected plants carefully away from field.

approved_chemical_options.active_ingredient: Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP or Dimethomorph 50% WP + Mancozeb or Metalaxyl-M 4% + Mancozeb 64% WP
approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Immediate curative/systemic + contact spray upon first symptom or local blight forecast alert
approved_chemical_options.cibrc_aligned_note: ICAR-CPRI recommended anti-oomycete fungicides for late blight.
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Late blight spreads explosively in fog/rain; never rely on single-site systemic fungicides alone (use co-formulations to prevent resistance). Verify label dosage & PHI with KVK.

region_notes.general: Explodes rapidly at 10–20°C with >80% humidity, fog, or winter drizzle.
region_notes.Indo-Gangetic Plains & Hills: Monitor ICAR-CPRI Indo-Blightcast alerts in UP, West Bengal, Bihar, Punjab, and hill regions.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate immediately to KVK/CPRI advisory on first blight detection during foggy/rainy weather to prevent total crop collapse.

symptoms: Dark brown to black circular/angular spots on older lower leaves displaying distinct concentric rings ('target-board' pattern).
Yellow chlorotic halo around lesions leading to premature defoliation of lower canopy.

severity_thresholds.moderate: 5%–20% leaf area affected progressing up to middle leaves.
severity_thresholds.severe: > 20% foliage blighted on middle/upper canopy prior to tuber bulking completion.

cultural_organic_control: Maintain balanced crop nutrition (adequate N and K) as nutrient-stressed plants suffer severe early blight.
Remove and compost/destroy infected crop debris after harvest and rotate with non-solanaceous crops (cereals/pulses).
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation late in the afternoon.

approved_chemical_options.active_ingredient: Mancozeb 75% WP or Chlorothalonil 75% WP or Azoxystrobin 23% SC
approved_chemical_options.target_stage: When concentric lesions spread upward onto middle leaves
approved_chemical_options.cibrc_aligned_note: CIB&RC-approved fungicides for Alternaria blight in potato.
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Ensure spray reaches lower and middle foliage. Verify exact CIB&RC label dilution, PHI, and PPE instructions with local KVK.

region_notes.general: Favored by warm temperatures (24–30°C) alternating with wet dew/irrigation cycles.
region_notes.Plains & Plateau Potato Belts: Common in mid-to-late crop stages across UP, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Karnataka.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate to KVK if upper canopy defoliation exceeds 20% during active tuber bulking.
disease_pest_cards.source_reference: ICAR-CPRI / DPPQS IPM Package for Potato

symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric target-board rings surrounded by yellow halos starting on older lower leaves.
Sunken dark leathery lesions may also develop near the stem-end calyx of fruits.

severity_thresholds.moderate: 5%–20% foliage affected spreading toward mid-canopy and fruit trusses.
severity_thresholds.severe: > 20% foliage defoliated or stem/fruit calyx lesions causing fruit drop.

cultural_organic_control: Prune and destroy heavily infected lower leaves touching soil and stake plants for airflow.
Apply organic mulch around base to prevent soil splash onto lower foliage during irrigation/rain.
Follow 2–3 year crop rotation away from tomato, potato, and brinjal.

approved_chemical_options.active_ingredient: Mancozeb 75% WP or Azoxystrobin 23% SC or Difenoconazole 25% EC
approved_chemical_options.target_stage: At initial upward spread from lower leaves to protect fruiting trusses
approved_chemical_options.cibrc_aligned_note: CIB&RC-registered fungicides for tomato Alternaria early blight.
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Strictly observe Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) on picking-stage tomato fruits! Verify label dilution and safe waiting days with KVK before application.

region_notes.general: Thrives in warm humid conditions (24–29°C) with frequent dew or drip/furrow splash.
region_notes.Maharashtra, Karnataka, AP & North India: Pervasive during post-monsoon and late-Rabi tomato harvests.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate to KVK if stem-collar cankers or >20% fruit/foliage loss threatens marketable harvest.
disease_pest_cards.source_reference: ICAR-IIHR / DPPQS IPM Package for Tomato

symptoms: Large, water-soaked greenish-black blotches on leaves and dark brown greasy streaks on stems.
Firm, dark brown greasy marbled rot on green fruits, with white mold visible in humid mornings.

severity_thresholds.moderate: 5%–15% foliage or stem streaks detected under cool wet weather.
severity_thresholds.severe: > 15% foliage/stem blight or active fruit rot across plants.

cultural_organic_control: Stake tomato plants, remove excess suckers for canopy ventilation, and avoid late-evening irrigation.
Promptly rogue and bury severely blighted stems/fruits away from the field.
Avoid planting tomato immediately adjacent to late-blight-infected potato fields.

approved_chemical_options.active_ingredient: Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP or Dimethomorph 50% WP + Mancozeb
approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Prompt intervention at first water-soaked lesion under cool humid forecasts
approved_chemical_options.cibrc_aligned_note: CIB&RC-aligned oomycete fungicide formulations for tomato.
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Observe strict Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) before harvesting tomatoes for consumption. Confirm label dilution and safe waiting period with local KVK.

region_notes.general: Cool wet weather (12–22°C, RH >85%) drives rapid stem and fruit collapse.
region_notes.Hills, North Plains & Western Ghats: High risk during winter rains and monsoon tomato cultivation.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate immediately to KVK if stem blight or fruit rot appears in cool humid weather.
disease_pest_cards.source_reference: ICAR-IIHR / DPPQS IPM Package for Tomato

symptoms: Severe upward curling and cupping of leaves, yellowing along leaf margins, and bushy stunted plant growth.
Drastic flower drop and miniature or absent fruit set.

severity_thresholds.low: < 5% plants infected with isolated whitefly vector presence.
severity_thresholds.severe: > 15% plants stunted with leaf curl prior to flowering.

cultural_organic_control: Rogue and destroy infected plants immediately (bag before pulling to avoid dispersing whiteflies), as viral diseases have NO chemical cure.
Raise nursery seedlings under insect-proof 40–50 mesh nylon net and plant resistant hybrids.
Install yellow sticky traps (20–30/ha) and spray Neem/NSKE 5% to deter the whitefly vector (Bemisia tabaci).

approved_chemical_options.active_ingredient: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL or Thiamethoxam 25% WG or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (Whitefly Vector Control Only)
approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Targeted ONLY against the whitefly vector on healthy/border plants when whiteflies are present; zero effect on virus itself
approved_chemical_options.cibrc_aligned_note: CIB&RC-registered vector insecticides; fungicides/bactericides cannot cure viruses.
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: NO pesticide cures Leaf Curl Virus. Never waste money spraying fungicides for viral curling. Manage whitefly vectors safely per KVK label dosage and observe strict PHI on fruiting crops.

region_notes.general: Transmitted exclusively by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci); worst in dry warm pre-monsoon/summer plantings.
region_notes.Karnataka, Maharashtra, AP & North Plain: Use ToLCV-tolerant hybrids and barrier border crops (maize/sorghum) around nurseries.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate to KVK if >15% nursery or early transplanted crop develops viral leaf curl for varietal and vector management advice.
disease_pest_cards.source_reference: ICAR-IIHR / DPPQS Tomato Leaf Curl IPM Guidelines

symptoms: Ragged elongated 'window-pane' feeding holes in whorl leaves with abundant sawdust-like moist frass inside the funnel.
Caterpillar has an inverted 'Y' marking on the head capsule and four square-arranged dark spots on the tail segment.

severity_thresholds.low: < 5% whorl-damaged plants with early pin-hole scraping.
severity_thresholds.moderate: 5%–10% whorl damage during early seedling-to-knee-high stage (ETL ~5–10% whorl infestation).
severity_thresholds.severe: > 10%–20% damaged whorls or cob/tassel boring by late-instar larvae.

cultural_organic_control: Install FAW pheromone traps (4–5/acre) right after germination and hand-crush visible egg masses/neonates.
Apply dry sand + lime/soil mixture or neem cake/ash into leaf whorls in small plots for mechanical/contact larval deterrence.
Spray Azadirachtin 1500 ppm or Metarhizium anisopliae / Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) directed straight into the whorl at egg hatch.

approved_chemical_options.active_ingredient: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC or Spinetoram 11.7% SC or Emamectin benzoate 5% SG
approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Direct whorl-targeted spray when >5–10% plants show fresh whorl damage
approved_chemical_options.cibrc_aligned_note: ICAR-IIMR / DPPQS ad-hoc CIB&RC recommended molecules for Fall Armyworm in maize.
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Target spray nozzle directly into leaf whorls during morning/evening hours; avoid spraying at peak bee pollen shedding. Verify exact label dilution and PHI with local KVK.

region_notes.general: Invasive polyphagous pest capable of defoliating maize within days if missed in the seedling-to-knee-high whorl stage.
region_notes.Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, MP &: High year-round pressure across Kharif, Rabi, and Spring maize belts.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate immediately to KVK if >15% whorls are heavily shredded or larvae begin boring into developing cobs.
disease_pest_cards.source_reference: ICAR-IIMR / DPPQS Fall Armyworm Management Advisory

symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped (elliptical) greyish-green to tan lesions (2.5–15 cm) running parallel to leaf veins.
Lesions coalesce to scorch whole lower leaves, starving grain fill if upper ear-leaf is hit.

severity_thresholds.low: < 5% leaf area affected restricted to lowest 2–3 leaves.
severity_thresholds.moderate: 5%–20% leaf area affected reaching middle leaves before tasseling.
severity_thresholds.severe: > 20% blight on ear leaf and upper foliage between tasseling and grain fill.

cultural_organic_control: Adopt resistant single-cross maize hybrids and practice deep ploughing/removal of infected maize stubble after harvest.
Rotate maize with non-host legumes or oilseeds to break residue-borne inoculum.
Maintain balanced potassium fertilization to improve foliar disease tolerance.

approved_chemical_options.active_ingredient: Mancozeb 75% WP or Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC
approved_chemical_options.target_stage: Protective spray if cigar-shaped lesions climb toward the ear leaf around pre-tasseling/silking
approved_chemical_options.cibrc_aligned_note: CIB&RC-aligned fungicide options for Turcicum leaf blight in maize.
approved_chemical_options.safety_warning: Verify exact CIB&RC label dilution, PHI, and safety equipment guidance with local KVK/DAO before spraying.

region_notes.general: Favored by moderate temperatures (18–27°C) and prolonged heavy dew or monsoon rains.
region_notes.Karnataka, Himachal, Bihar & J&K: Endemic in humid hill regions and winter/Rabi maize pockets.

disease_pest_cards.kvk_escalation_trigger: Escalate to KVK if cigar-shaped lesions reach the ear leaf before silking/grain filling.
disease_pest_cards.source_reference: ICAR-IIMR / DPPQS Maize Disease Management Package
